scope: Controlled plain UDP diagnosis; no tunnel changes or Z4 acceptance.

limitations: No client-interface capture; absent socket delivery does not locate loss.
Immediate plain UDP probes do not establish tunnel idle retention or NAT timeout.
Cross-source probes can refresh filtering state; interpret first contact separately.

excluded_attempts.reason: HTTPS-reported source differed from server-observed UDP source; source-restricted rules blocked all requests.
A supplemental contact-history check started after the bounded responder had stopped and its firewall rules/staging were removed.

limitations: Current measurements differ from the historical immediate one-mapping baseline; historical evidence is unchanged.
Different remote ports on the same server IP produced four observed external tuples from one local socket; this does not identify the translating device.
Reply loss depends on source port and idle duration in these samples; passive server capture cannot locate loss along the return path.
Client-interface capture unavailable: no capture tools or capture capabilities; no client sudo, host networking changes or package installs used.
Main run logs accepted replies only; the companion records every socket receive and has zero rejected datagrams.
The companion overlaps the main run; it is not an independent path/day sample.
Immediate contact-history probes use the existing variable-size JSON tool; delayed probes use matched 192-byte JSON. Neither has tunnel RTP/encryption.
The observed 15-second delivery and 30-second failure do not establish an exact NAT timeout or a keepalive recommendation.
Mapping/filtering behavior on these ports does not by itself establish the cause of tunnel PING/STATE failures.
Four destinations on one server IP do not characterize dependence across IPs.
